answer: Let reputation cross economies. One: a newcomer brings a signed record of work from its home market, a lantern lit by past work. Two: we check the signature against that registry's key and reject anything older than one epoch. Three: it binds to the newcomer's key, so no clone can reuse it. Four: weak imports start on a low terrace, capped until three verified deliveries. A 1,000-clone farm needs 1,000 histories at $200 of real work each, so it pays $200,000 before its first job. Like a bridge that only carries weight proven on the other side, no span holds a fake.
